shot: Close on a garment tag turning in a hand. A certification seal fills the frame, crisp and official, then the wearer zips the jacket and walks out of shot. Daylight, shallow focus.
notes: An unnamed seal shown as an achieved certification. Sources: Fair Trade USA covers the Portugal factory only; Sri Lanka is in process; B Corp is pending.
label: supported
judge_explanation: A viewer would wrongly conclude that the garment carries a specific official certification seal, even though the shot does not identify a certification that the sources confirm applies to that garment.

shot: A conveyor of returned garments runs the length of the frame, each one lifted and placed into a single bin marked for reuse, nothing left behind. Camera tracks the full line end to end. Clean overhead light.
notes: Shows every returned garment being reused. Sources: Take Back disposition is 61% recycled, 31% donated, 8% landfilled.
label: unsupported
judge_explanation: The full conveyor ending with every returned garment placed into one reuse bin and “nothing left behind” would imply all take-back garments are reused or diverted from landfill, whereas the sources state 8% are landfilled and only 61% are recycled into industrial fiber.

shot: Extreme close-up of knit fabric stretching under two thumbs, individual fibres separating in the light, then snapping back flat. Camera holds at hand height, shallow depth of field. Low side light, film grain.
notes: Material texture only. Asserts nothing about scale, certification or completeness.
label: supported
judge_explanation: The shot shows fabric and its visible movement without depicting certifications, sustainability claims, or an undocumented brand-wide process.

shot: A runner slows on a wet trail, shrugs off a worn forest-green jacket with a mended elbow and hands it to a second runner, who pulls it on and continues. One unbroken waist-height tracking shot. Overcast afternoon light.
notes: A garment passed from one wearer to another. Depicts reuse as an act, without quantifying it or implying a programme outcome.
label: supported
judge_explanation: A viewer would wrongly conclude that Verdant operates or supports a direct garment handoff/reuse program in which worn items are passed on and kept in use.

shot: Rain beads on a jacket shoulder, then slides off as the wearer turns into the wind. Camera at shoulder height, handheld, holding on the fabric surface. Flat grey daylight, no sun.
notes: Water behaviour on fabric. The product catalogue describes the Watershed Jacket as water-resistant, not waterproof — check whether the shot reads as either.
label: unsupported
judge_explanation: The viewer would not wrongly conclude any unsubstantiated brand fact; it simply shows a jacket shedding rain in use.
